Of course! Here’s a recipe for Bourekas, a dish of pastries filled with cheese. I’ve included a list of ingredients you should always have on hand, and a list of instructions for making the filling and the pastries.

Ingredients:
-1 cup of milk (any kind, I use whole milk)
-1 cup of grated asiago cheese
-1 cup of grated sharp cheddar cheese
-6-8 cups of cake flour
-2/3 cup of milk
-a pinch of salt
-1/4 tsp of baking powder
-1/4 tsp of baking soda
-1 cup of grated parmesan
-1/4 cup of chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:

1. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Grease an 8” x 11” baking pan with non-stick cooking spray.
2. In a medium saucepan, combine all milk and cheese. Over medium heating, stir until the cheese is melted. (The heat should be low and the milk warm, not piping hot).
3. Remove from heat and add the baking powder and salt.
4. Pour into the prepared pan and sprinkle with the parmesan and parsley.
5. In the same saucepan over medium heat, mix together the flour and the milk mixture. Stir constantly while adding to the saucepan. If you have a whisk you will save a lot of time. Once you get to the end of the flour mixture, you should not be able to see any flour. (There is no longer any water left in the saucepan) Turn to low heat and continue stirring until the mixture forms a ball.
6. Turn off heat and add enough milk to create a dough. If you are using cake flour, you only need to add a little milk and it will come together. Use a little extra flour if the dough is too sticky.
7. Put the dough back into the saucepan and add the parmesan and parsley. Fold and knead the dough for a minute or two.
8. On a lightly floured surface, divide the dough in half. With one half, fold it so that it touches the edge of the pan. (It will stick, which is okay.) This is your top half. With the other half, fold it so that it touches the bottom half. This is your bottom half. Knead for a minute.
9. Cover the pan and leave it to rest at room temperature for 1 hour. It will become very sticky.
10. After 1 hour, turn the dough over and knead briefly for 1 minute. The dough should be smooth and free of holes and cracks, but it is still sticky. 
11. Roll out the dough on a lightly floured surface to at least 1/4″ thick. (It should be about 1/8″ thick.) Cut it into your desired shapes.
12. Prick the tops of the pastries with a fork.
13. Heat the baking pan over medium-high heat and add some butter so that the butter melts and coats the bottom of the pan.
14. Place the pastries in the pan and spray the top with non-stick cooking spray, again to make sure it doesn’t stick.
15. Bake for 15-18 minutes or until the tops are golden brown. The cheese should be hot as you take it out of the oven. Serve warm.
